blocks.text:
After breakfast we’re going to city tour. Santiago has some of the most eye-catching scenery in Latin America, with the city surrounded on all sides by the Andes Mountains. Huge skyscrapers rise up from the ground, and the city stretches outwards as far as the eye can see. After breakfast in your hotel, take this chance to go on a tour of the historical center, stopping first at the Plaza de Armas, a huge square that transports you back to the colonial days. You can imagine the bustling markets, merchants and soldiers wandering the cobbled stones of what was and remains the central hub of the city. The square is home to several monuments, such as to the founder of Santiago, Pedro de Valdivia, as well as the Royal Palace, the Metropolitan Cathedral of Santiago and the Central Post Office Building.

After the excursion you will be transferred back to the hotel.

In the second part of the day you can order extra tour Maipo Valley ($175 per person, minimum 2PAX)

Discover the traditions of Chilean winemaking on a delightful journey to the Maipo Valley. Visit one renowned winery, explore its vineyards and cellars, and learn about the region’s iconic varietals. Enjoy a guided tasting of premium wines while taking in the beautiful Andean scenery — a perfect introduction to one of Chile’s most celebrated wine regions.

blocks.text:
Free day in Santiago. You can order extra tour Valparaiso ($260 per person, minimum 2PAX)

Valparaíso, Chile, offers a perfect mix of history, culture, and stunning views for a one-day visit. Start your day with breakfast at Café de la Plaza, located in the heart of the city, where you can enjoy a traditional Chilean breakfast with coffee and fresh pastries. Afterward, take a stroll through the UNESCO-listed historic center, wandering through the colorful streets and admiring the vibrant murals and colonial architecture. Head to Plaza Sotomayor to learn about the city’s maritime history before hopping on one of the iconic funiculars that take you up the hills surrounding Valparaíso. The ride offers spectacular views of the city and the harbor, and you can stop at one of the many viewpoints to capture the scenic landscape.

Next, visit La Sebastiana, the former home of poet Pablo Neruda. The quirky house is filled with art, antiques, and offers panoramic views of the city. After, take a relaxing walk along Paseo 21 de Mayo, a scenic promenade offering fantastic views of Valparaíso's hills and the port.

In the afternoon, visit the Museo de Bellas Artes to enjoy Chilean art and more stunning views of the bay. Conclude your day by heading to Playa Ancha, a quieter beach area perfect for watching the sunset over the Pacific Ocean.
